title: Grateful Dead Live at Fieldhouse, University of Iowa on 1973-02-24

ai_review.summary: Stunning soundboard capture of a legendary Phil Lesh bass jam with crystal‑clear treble and booming stereo bass, though only a short fragment is available.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers an exceptionally clear soundboard mix that showcases Phil's soaring, stereo‑spread bass solo—often dubbed “The Phil Zone”—with crisp highs and punchy lows. Reviewers rave about the jam’s inventive flow (Truckin → Nobody’s Fault → Phil solo) and its place leading into a Sugar Magnolia segment, even though the fragment is only ~9 minutes long.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly high reviewer scores (average ≈ 4.7) and consistent praise for both the musical performance and the superb soundboard quality outweigh the limitation of a short fragment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp treble, crunchy bass, excellent stereo imaging of Phil's bass (Wall‑of‑Sound effect captured). No noted dropouts; only drawback is the very short length of the fragment.

standout_songs: Phil Lesh Bass Solo (often called “The Phil Zone”)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Fragment focuses on a high‑energy jam that moves from Truckin' into Nobody's Fault, then launches into an extended Phil solo before segueing toward Sugar Magnolia. Reviewers love the flow but lament the missing surrounding material.

band_member_comments.Phil: Multiple reviewers highlight the amazing stereo bass sound, Wall‑of‑Sound separation of strings, and the sheer creativity of his solo.
